tokenScopeNote: its dark look declares its own variables on html.t4-dark[data-style=terminal] (0,2,1), above the family's html.t4-dark: the last selector lets the system's values and the template variables below win there, on the same element
modesNote: the template has a light/dark switch (.kinetic-theme-toggle in the header; js/darkmode.js and the pre-paint resolver in index.php set data-theme light|dark on html, and t4-dark on the dark side; ?theme=light|dark on the address): the module sheet writes the system's own side under the template's matching mode and the other side derived from it (src/derive.mjs, src/sides.mjs), and does not hide the switch (Akemi 13/10/2026: hiding it is a bug; MODE-2). Without it the Design system preview offered no Light | Dark for JA Kinetic Joomla while its WordPress twin did (14/10/2026)
modesAutoNote: the pre-paint resolver in index.php always sets data-theme (light or dark, from the cookie, ?theme= or the template's default) before the page paints, so no 'auto' state is left to the OS: the OS-dark copy is not written, and the module stays under its 64 KB column (85 KB with it, 14/10/2026)
modeHookNote: js/darkmode.js and the pre-paint resolver in index.php mark the dark side with three marks on the root, set and cleared together: data-theme="dark", data-bs-theme="dark" (the Bootstrap colour-mode rules template.css carries, 29 of them) and the class t4-dark (the template and darkmode sheets key almost every dark rule on html.t4-dark, 79 selectors; light on html:not(.t4-dark)). The slot sides and the Design system popup Light | Dark read and set all three (src/sides.mjs, design-system-live-page.js). With the default data-theme hook a press set only data-theme: the template opens dark, so Light left t4-dark and data-bs-theme=dark on the page (header switch showing the dark side icon, headings in the dark side weight and grey, the integrations icons in the dark side lime on the light page; reproduced in the live frame on the published 1.0.8, 18/10/2026), and a page opened light (cookie or ?theme=light) pressed Dark got the system dark colours over the template light rules. Same marks and fix as the WordPress twin (d2aa12a507). The flow turns a hooked page with its own switch (selectors.themeToggle, .kinetic-theme-toggle in the header and the drawer), as a visitor does: without it the flow found no switch and left the page on the template dark side under every light system (MODE-1).
templateNote: JA Kinetic acceptance (14/10/2026): --elevated and --chrome-elevated (the timeline band, the closing card and the footer) take the system's quiet raised surface, surface-warm, as the WordPress twin's theme maps them: on the card surface they stood as grey blocks on Moxie's black page (loud-band, GROUND-2). Two-mode preview (14/10/2026): the light look writes --surface and --chrome-surface as literal #FFFFFF (its dark look reads var(--ds-c-surface)); the preview frame runs no script, so its dark side has data-theme but no t4-dark and kept the light look's white: the closing card faded from the system's ground to white (gradient-stop): both follow the system surface on either look. JA Kinetic paints with its own variables, and its dark look (the default) leaves four of them literal: --elevated #0F1311 (the incident-timeline and call-to-action bands), --muted and --chrome-muted #7F8B86 (labels, footer text) and --primary-ink #0A0D0C (text on its lime buttons). Under a light system the bands stayed near-black while their text took the system's dark text (1.11:1 under Apple), the footer's grey sat on the system's light chrome (2.96:1 under MotherDuck) and dark ink sat on Apple's blue (4.16:1; round-3 probe, 11/10/2026): the bands take the surface, the greys the system muted, the ink the accent's own text colour --heading takes the system text colour, var(--ds-c-fg): the template reads its headings from fg-2, its brighter heading colour, while the slot fg-2 is a softer secondary text, so every heading read quieter than the body under a system (HIER-2 heading-quiet, 82 issues, 15/10/2026).
followNote: its eyebrows (each block's own: hx, bento, clients, split, testimonials, call to action, sign-in), timeline times, metrics badge and article links are text in var(--primary), the system accent: MotherDuck's sky blue on its cream, 1.62:1: they take the readable accent; the KineticQL call to action writes its own dark ink (--split-primary-ink, declared on the block) on the accent: it takes the accent's own text colour The Signal home (body.site-signal) paints its page and content column in a hair-lifted tint the auto palette reads as the card surface: under a dark system the whole page stood 1.21:1 off its header and bands; it takes the page ground. The FAQ support band takes the quiet raised surface, as the other bands do (GROUND-2 loud-band, 15/10/2026). The Integrations page's closing call-to-action bar (.acm-cta.cta-bar .hx-section, page-219.css) paints its section in var(--ds-c-ink) while html carries .t4-dark (the template's own dark side, its default, which the class keeps in the Add site preview and on a site whose visitor stays dark under a light system) and var(--ds-c-bg) otherwise; the template draws it level with its page (1.00:1), but under a system ink is the system's text (light) or its lifted ink (dark): Moxie made it a pitch-black band under its light side and a grey one under its dark side (GROUND-2 loud-band, probe v10, 18/10/2026). It takes the page ground on both sides.

pictureRulesNote: 20/10/2026 (PIC-1): the Integrations page (/index.php/product/integrations, module [Kinetic] Integrations - Logos, acm clients style-2) shows ten line icons as SVGs stroked in the template lime #A3E635 (light: olive through a brightness filter): a worn system cannot reach inside a picture, so they stayed lime under every system. Under a system each icon is drawn as a mask (an inline percent-encoded copy of its own file, so it fetches nothing) painted with the accent text role (the picture itself pushed out of its box, the light-side filter dropped); the shared block names the ten files, so a card image the customer changes keeps its own look. No system worn: nothing of this is written (DEF-1). 20/10/2026: three demo pictures of the home are rasters drawn in the template lime, owner-swappable media fields whose template defaults are images/kinetic/*.webp: the hero terminal (LIVE dot and word, the highlighted bar of the sparkline), the KineticQL code panel (the query keywords) and the bento telemetry chart in content (the chip, the metrics line, the trace bar). Under Moxie and Figma they stayed lime (eye check; no detector named it). Under a system the box of each one lays two layers over the picture, which stays under them with its alt text: a ::before patch in the picture's own ground (title bar #111514, body #0c110f, chart #161c18) hides the lime and its anti-aliased edge, a ::after shape painted with --ds-c-accent-on-ink (the accent readable on a dark panel) draws the same marks; both shapes are inline SVG masks (the WordPress twin's geometry, theme 1.1.19). The layers sit at z-index 1 in the box's own stacking context (isolation): the hero and code-panel pictures carry a drop-shadow filter, which makes them a layer painted over a ::before at auto. The status colours (INFO, WARN, ERROR, the timings) and the window dots are the picture's own and stay. Only the template's own files are matched: the hero and code-panel boxes need all three direction pictures (terminal, blueprint, signal) to be the template's, the chart its own file; a picture the owner swapped keeps its look. The chart's hue filter of the Blueprint and Signal homes is dropped under a system, as the overlay already paints the system's accent. No system worn: nothing of this is written (DEF-1).
literalsNote: The patches under the three demo pictures' recoloured marks (pictureRules ::before) are painted in each picture's own ground, so the lime they hide leaves no edge: the terminal window's title bar #111514 and body #0c110f, the telemetry chart's #161c18. They are colours of the template's own pictures, not of the page, and sit under the system's accent only.
